notes: Two fixes that say the same thing: what Sonos reports outranks what the app remembers. FROZEN TRACK -- a radio zone kept showing whatever song was playing when the station started. Observed live with Master Bedroom on iHeart Lost 80s, Sonos reporting Eurythmics then Prince while the app showed Chaka Khan from several tracks earlier. The reducer treated a declaration confirmed by URI as authoritative over polling, which is sound for a local file whose URI changes with every track and false for a stream whose URI is the STATION and never changes while the songs do. The authority boundary is now compositional: the app supplies only what Sonos cannot report (station name and logo, local album art), Sonos supplies track and artist via r:streamContent. STOPPED ZONES -- the reducer returned the stored last-playing outright and never reached the line returning what polling had just resolved, so every poll resolved a stopped zone's parked URI correctly and the answer was discarded. Fixed by deleting the early return; the stored copy now serves only its real purpose, a zone Sonos cannot describe at all. This matters most for content started in the Sonos app, which appeared correctly while playing and reverted to Sorriva's own older memory the moment it stopped. PHASE C CLOSED AS NOT NEEDED, a negative result worth recording: its premise -- that an ungrouped zone wrongly reports pre-grouping content -- was asserted from reading code and is wrong. Querying the speakers settled it in one command: a grouped member never receives the stream (its transport points at the coordinator via x-rincon:), its own queue is untouched throughout, and Sonos restores it on separation. Measured with Patio coordinating Bossa Beyond and Garage separating still parked on its own Lost 80s. So the old behaviour was correct -- what an ungrouped zone reports is what will actually play. The projection built against that premise was removed. Kept from the work: Stop after becomeCoordinator on each separation path, and contentDeclaration(forZoneID:) as one resolution order with transferPlayback's three inline branches collapsed onto it. Verified on device across station-to-station, station-to-local, local-to-station and local-to-local. Newly logged and not fixed: the station resolve cache is not holding (every zone re-resolves every poll), and the Xcode restructure that makes new source files require manual project edits.
